SOURCE: "Smarter, Better, Faster, Longer: A Modern Bidirectional Encoder for Fast, Memory Efficient, and Long Context Finetuning and Inference" (ModernBERT), Benjamin Warner, Antoine Chaffin, Benjamin Clavié, Orion Weller, Oskar Hallström, Said Taghadouini, Alexis Gallagher, Raja Biswas, Faisal Ladhak, Tom Aarsen, Nathan Cooper, Griffin Adams, Jeremy Howard, Iacopo Poli (Answer.AI, LightOn, JHU, NVIDIA, HuggingFace). Preprint, arXiv:2412.13663v2, 19 Dec 2024.

COVERAGE: 84,012 of 84,012 chars; all 20 pages read, including Limitations (p. 9), Appendices A–G (pp. 15–20) with Tables 3–11. References (pp. 10–15) skimmed for origins only. Extraction clean.

File: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/generative-ai/02-rag-retrieval/sources/warner-2024-smarter-better-faster-longer.pdf

CLAIMS (ranked)

- claim: ModernBERT is a pretrained MLM *backbone*, not an off-the-shelf embedder; every retrieval number is after contrastive fine-tuning on MS MARCO.
  number: 1.25M samples, batch 16 (DPR); 810k samples (ColBERT)
  setup: all base models fine-tuned identically with sentence-transformers (DPR, mined hard negatives) or PyLate (ColBERT, KL distillation from BGE-M3 teacher)
  quote: "We train every base model using the MS-MARCO (Bajaj et al., 2016) dataset with mined hard negatives (Xuan et al., 2020) on 1.25M samples with a batch size of 16" / "Models are trained on 810k samples from MS-Marco (Bajaj et al., 2016) and teacher scores from BGE-M3 (Chen et al., 2024), using the PyLate library"
  where: p. 5

- claim: On BEIR (nDCG@10, 15-dataset average) ModernBERT edges every compared encoder in both single-vector and multi-vector settings, but the DPR margin over GTE-en-MLM-base is 0.2 points.
  number: DPR base 41.6 vs GTE 41.4, NomicBERT 41.0, BERT 38.9, RoBERTa 37.7, DeBERTaV3 20.2; DPR large 44.0 vs GTE 42.5, RoBERTa 41.4; ColBERT base 51.3 vs NomicBERT 49.9, BERT 49.0; ColBERT large 52.4 vs GTE 50.7
  setup: Table 1; BEIR 15 datasets; LR swept over 6 values and chosen on NFCorpus/SciFact/TREC-Covid/FiQA subset
  quote: "ModernBERT 41.6 27.4 44.0 51.3 80.2 88.4 56.4 73.6" (base row) ; "ModernBERT 44.0 34.3 48.6 52.4 80.4 90.4 59.5 83.9" (large row) ; "While ModernBERT-base only narrowly edges out GTE-en-MLM-base on DPR evaluations"
  where: p. 6

- claim: The BEIR average leans heavily on TREC-COVID; per-dataset, ModernBERT-base DPR loses to GTE-en-MLM-base on 8 of 15 datasets.
  number: TREC-Covid 72.1 (ModernBERT-base) vs 49.7 (GTE-base); 74.1 vs 48.4 at large. ModernBERT-base DPR below GTE-base on NFCorpus (23.7 vs 26.3), FiQA (28.8 vs 30.1), Climate-FEVER, DBPedia (23.8 vs 28.9), FEVER (59.9 vs 66.5), HotpotQA (46.1 vs 49.9), MSMARCO (61.6 vs 63.1), NQ (39.5 vs 41.7), SciDocs
  setup: Table 7, single-vector nDCG@10
  quote: "ModernBERT 23.7 57.0 72.1 28.8 35.7 23.6 23.8 59.9 46.1 61.6 39.5 85.9 12.5 20.8 33.1 41.6" ; "it should be noted that an important factor in its performance is TREC-COVID (Voorhees et al., 2021), potentially showcasing the benefits of ModernBERT being trained with a more recent knowledge cutoff than most existing encoders. However, NomicBERT and GTE have also been trained on updated data, so the cutoff cannot be the only factor"
  where: Table 7 p. 19; text p. 18

- claim: Multi-vector (ColBERT) models generalise to 8192-token documents without long-context fine-tuning; single-vector models need it.
  number: MLDR OOD ColBERT: ModernBERT 80.2 (base) / 80.4 (large) vs GTE 69.3/71.3, NomicBERT 61.3, BERT 28.1. MLDR OOD DPR: ModernBERT-base 27.4 vs GTE-base 34.3; in-domain 44.0 vs 44.4
  setup: Table 1; MLDR English subset (>200k long docs), nDCG@10; OOD = trained only on short MS MARCO
  quote: "without long-context finetuning ModernBERT outperforms both shorter-context models and the long-context NomicBERT but performs noticeably worse than GTE-en-MLM. The performance gap narrows considerably when evaluated in-domain" ; "long-context models (GTE-en-MLM, NomicBERT, and ModernBERT) all outperform short-context models by at least 40 NDCG@10 points without requiring any specific finetuning"
  where: p. 7

- claim: Long-context throughput: ModernBERT is 2.65x (base) and 3x (large) faster than the next-fastest encoder at 8192 tokens, on one RTX 4090.
  number: 8192 fixed: ModernBERT-base 123.7k tok/s vs GTE 46.8k, NomicBERT 46.1k; large 46.8k vs GTE 16.2k. 512 fixed: ModernBERT-base 148.1k vs BERT 180.4k, RoBERTa 179.9k, GTE 123.7k, DeBERTaV3 70.2k. Variable-length: ModernBERT-base 147.3k vs GTE+xformers 128.6k
  setup: Table 2, thousands of tokens/s, 8192 synthetic docs per set, averaged over 10 runs, single NVIDIA RTX 4090; BERT/RoBERTa/DeBERTa cannot run 8192
  quote: "ModernBERT 149M 1604 148.1 147.3 98 123.7 133.8" ; "All efficiency evaluations are ran on a single NVIDIA RTX 4090" ; "processes fixed-length 512 token inputs faster than all other recent encoders, although slower than the original BERT and RoBERTa models" ; "processing documents 2.65 and 3 times faster than the next-fastest encoder at the BASE and LARGE sizes"
  where: p. 7–8

- claim: Memory: ModernBERT-base fits batches twice as large as any other base model; large fits 60% more than other large models but less than BERT-large at 512.
  number: max BS 512 tokens: ModernBERT-base 1604 vs BERT 1096, GTE 640, DeBERTaV3 236; 8192: 98 vs 38 (GTE). Large: 770 vs BERT-large 792
  setup: Table 2, RTX 4090
  quote: "ModernBERT-base is able to process batch sizes twice as large as every other model on both input lengths. ModernBERT-large is slightly less memory efficient than the original BERT-large on short-context inputs, but can process batches at least 60 percent bigger than every other large model."
  where: p. 8

- claim: GLUE: ModernBERT-base is the first MLM-trained encoder to beat DeBERTaV3-base; large is second to DeBERTaV3-large.
  number: base 88.4 vs DeBERTaV3 88.1, RoBERTa 86.4, BERT 84.7; large 90.4 vs DeBERTaV3-large 91.4, RoBERTa 88.9
  setup: Table 1 / Table 5, GLUE dev set averages, per-task hyperparameter sweep; prior models' numbers taken from literature
  quote: "ModernBERT-base surpasses all existing base models, including DeBERTaV3-base, becoming the first MLM-trained model to do so" ; "ModernBERT-large is the second-best large encoder on GLUE, almost matching DeBERTaV3-large with one-tenth fewer parameters while processing tokens in half the time"
  where: p. 7

- claim: Code retrieval is where the lead is largest, because it is the only compared encoder pretrained on code.
  number: CodeSearchNet 56.4 vs 44.9 (GTE-base); StackQA 73.6 vs 71.4; large 59.5 / 83.9 vs 47.3 / 68.1 (RoBERTa-large)
  setup: Table 1, CoIR framework, single-vector; StackQA docs average >2000 tokens
  quote: "This result was expected, as it is the only evaluated encoder to be trained on a data mixture including programming data."
  where: p. 7

- claim: Training recipe: 2T tokens, primarily English, 1024 context for 1.7T tokens then extended to 8192 over 300B tokens; 30% masking; no NSP.
  number: 149M / 395M params, 22 / 28 layers; 8x H100; base 194 h, large 425 h pretraining
  setup: Table 3
  quote: "Both ModernBERT models are trained on 2 trillion tokens of primarily English data" ; "After training on 1.7 trillion tokens at a 1024 sequence length and RoPE theta of 10,000, we extend the native context length of ModernBERT to 8192 tokens" ; "Training Hardware 8x H100" ; "use a masking rate of 30 percent, as the original rate of 15 percent has since been shown to be sub-optimal"
  where: p. 3–4, Table 3 p. 16

- claim: Alternating global/local attention (global every 3rd layer, 128-token local window) cost nothing in downstream quality in ablation.
  number: every third layer global; 128-token window; RoPE theta 160,000 global / 10,000 local
  setup: ablation at 100B tokens
  quote: "This setup yielded identical downstream performance when compared to the use of global attention in every layer, even at 100 billion tokens, while resulting in major speedups."
  where: p. 17

- claim: DeBERTaV3 is strong on GLUE but collapses on retrieval and is 5–7x more memory-hungry.
  number: BEIR DPR 20.2 (base) / 25.6 (large)
  quote: "DeBERTaV3's memory use is 5-to-7 times higher than ModernBERT's, and it processes inputs, two times slower"
  where: p. 18

LIMITS
- Not an embedding model: the released weights are an MLM backbone. The note's "A real embedder" section uses BGE; ModernBERT would need the DPR fine-tune described above before cosine search works. The paper gives no MTEB score and no zero-shot embedding result.
- English only: "This study focuses exclusively on the English language... not directly applicable to other languages, and potentially even less-so to lower resources languages" (p. 9).
- Single-vector long-context is the weak spot: loses to GTE-en-MLM OOD on MLDR (27.4 vs 34.3 base); authors say it "may require more adapted tuning" and leave the cause (local attention vs GTE's longer-context pretraining budget) to future work (p. 7).
- Short-context throughput is below original BERT/RoBERTa (148k vs 180k tok/s at 512).
- BEIR lead is small and TREC-COVID-driven; loses to GTE-base on most individual BEIR datasets in the DPR setting.
- GLUE baselines are copied from literature, not re-run; GTE GLUE numbers taken from GTE's own paper after an inconsistent sweep (footnote 7).
- Efficiency on one consumer GPU (RTX 4090) only; no CPU, no A100/H100 numbers reported.
- Authors concede MLM-only objective may trail RTD for classification, and parameter scaling unexplored (p. 9).
- No figures at all; all evidence is in tables.
- Dated: v2 Dec 2024; concurrent GTE-en-MLM and NomicBERT are the only long-context comparators.

BUILDS ON
- BERT (Devlin et al., 2019); MosaicBERT (Portes et al., 2023) codebase and MLM setup; CrammingBERT (Geiping and Goldstein, 2023).
- DPR (Karpukhin et al., 2020) and ColBERT (Khattab and Zaharia, 2020) for the two retrieval settings; ColBERTv2 (Santhanam et al., 2022) and JaColBERTv2.5 (Clavié, 2024) training recipe; BGE-M3 (Chen et al., 2024) as teacher; BEIR (Thakur et al., 2021); MLDR (Chen et al., 2024); CoIR (Li et al., 2024).
- RoPE (Su et al., 2024); GeGLU (Shazeer, 2020); sliding-window attention (Beltagy et al., 2020) and alternation (Gemma 2, 2024); unpadding (Zeng et al., 2022); Flash Attention 2/3 (Dao 2023; Shah et al., 2024); hardware-aware design (Anthony et al., 2024); OLMo tokenizer (Groeneveld et al., 2024); StableAdamW (Wortsman et al., 2023); WSD schedule (Hägele et al., 2024); 30% masking (Wettig et al., 2023); Phi-style weight tiling (Li et al., 2023).
- Code: https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/ModernBERT, Apache 2.0 (p. 1, p. 19).
